mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or registrar of companies in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, obtain one apostille from the designated competent authority in that state; if the issuing state is not a party, use the parallel track of notarization, competent ministry authentication, and legalization by the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate. The two tracks are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, commercial register, or competent company law registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the designated competent authority if the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state; otherwise consular legalization through the Korean mission after ministry of foreign affairs authentication. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing subscription of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporator and counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner entity, executed by registered directors and notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of director signatures followed by either a sole Hague apostille for Apostille Convention states or a sole Korean consular legalization for non-member states; only one authentication path is used depending on the issuing country, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association, Charter, or Memorandum and Articles of Association of the foreign corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified source from the corporate registry or the registered office of the corporate shareholder, authenticated by the company secretary or registered legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy path: registry certification, then Hague apostille if the issuing state is an Apostille member; if not, consular legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and are not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and source-of-funds confirmation issued by the ultimate beneficial owner's financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified commercial bank or financial institution where the corporate shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner maintains its primary settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank letterhead, signature notarized, then either Hague apostille for Apostille Convention countries or Korean consular legalization for non-member states. The chosen path is final and cannot be chained with the other.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before accepting any foreign investor, the firm must screen every individual and legal entity against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit PEP database, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK Sanctions List, and KoFIU domestic alerts. Screening must cover all shareholders, directors, signatories, authorized agents, and beneficial owners at or above 25%. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs and close associates; source of funds and source of wealth must be evidenced through audited financials or bank statements. Negative hits require suspension of the formation process, a documented risk decision, and, where required, a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU within the statutorily prescribed business days. All screening results shall be archived with timestamps and search criteria.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (I-RO) of the Supreme Court of Korea; official electronic corporate trade-name search and reservation portal (iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be written in Korean (Hangeul) and must contain Yuhan Hoesa as the mandatory limited-company suffix. If the brand is foreign, the registry requires a complete phonetic transliteration into Hangeul; English can be displayed in financial and commercial documents but does not replace the Hangeul legal name. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) distinctive brand or geographic element; (2) object of business; (3) optional qualifier such as Digital Content or Audio Licensing; and (4) statutory legal-form marker Yuhan Hoesa. Latin and Hangeul characters cannot be freely mixed in the registered legal name unless the registry accepts a full phonetic transliteration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Korea (when used to imply state sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a name rejection notice, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the district registry or the Supreme Court Registry Information Center under the Administrative Procedures Act, attaching the rejected trade name, the statutory basis for objection, and any ministerial approval for sensitive tokens. If the rejection is based on an identical or confusingly similar registered trade name in the same business sector, the applicant may submit the prior registrant's written consent or evidence of deregistration and non-use. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may institute administrative litigation in the local district court within 90 days after service while reserving a substitute name through the I-RO portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not acceptable as the sole registered office for this royalty-free stock-music licensing company if banking and tax substance are required. The National Tax Service and commercial banks treat a shared mailbox as high risk for VAT and corporate income tax registration because they demand an actual place of management, a lease contract in the company's name, utility invoices, and access to books. For a remote digital licensing business, a serviced office or the local representative's physical domestic address is strongly preferred; pure virtual office may be permissible for company registration only, but banks will likely reject the customer due diligence and anti-money laundering stage and the tax office may deny business-site presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 25% to 35% unannounced physical inspection within the first two assessment years. Checklist for de facto place of business: (1) nameplate on the premises; (2) written lease with the company as tenant; (3) electricity and telecom bills in the company name; (4) one or more local employees or administrative director with payroll records; (5) segregated server logs or hard-copy books; (6) board minutes kept at the address; (7) tax invoices issued from Korea; (8) active bank account statements matching the invoicing system. The local tax office or registry may conduct an unannounced site visit when a company files zero-tax returns, shows a revenue and physical-presence mismatch, or records high-volume digital subscriptions without demonstrating local operational substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part IV on Yuhan Hoesa, Articles 543 et seq., covering formation, contribution obligations, director appointment, representation, and registration of a limited liability company; read together with the Commercial Registration Act for filing procedures and registration efficacies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's principal office in the Republic of Korea (Deunggi-gwa), operating through the National Court Administration's Registration Bureau
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Registration (beopin deunggi sincheongseo) accompanied by the notarized articles of incorporation, capital contribution proof, director consent documents, corporate seal specimen, and registered office lease confirmation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is mandated by the Commercial Act. The articles of incorporation must state the total capital and each member's contribution amount; all contributions must be fully paid or performed before the corporate registration is made. The paid-in capital may be kept in a Korean bank contribution deposit account established in the name of the proposed company or its representative director. This account is not a blocked escrow, but the funds must remain deposited and dedicated to the Company until the incorporation registration is completed. After registration, the Company has unrestricted use of the contributed capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001. FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (KOREA). WHEREAS, the undersigned directors have been validly named as the initial directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), a limited liability company formed under Part IV of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (the Act); WHEREAS, the articles of incorporation of the Company have been executed by all initial members and notarized by a notary public in the Republic of Korea; WHEREAS, each member has contributed in full the cash or in-kind property set opposite his or her name in the articles of incorporation; WHEREAS, the person named in the articles of incorporation as representative director has accepted that appointment. NOW, THEREFORE, the undersigned directors, acting unanimously by written resolution in lieu of a formal board meeting as permitted by the articles and the Act, do hereby resolve and record as follows. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The Company's stated capital as recorded in the articles of incorporation is approved, ratified, and confirmed. Each member's contribution obligation is declared satisfied with respect to the cash or property actually paid or contributed before the effective date of this resolution. The representative director shall preserve the deposit certificate and all transfer deeds, shall register the capital amount in the commercial registry, and shall cause contribution records to be maintained. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Company shall establish and maintain a corporate current account at a licensed Korean commercial bank selected by the management. The representative director, together with any co-signatory named in the written bank mandate, is authorized to open and operate the account, endorse checks, instruct remittances, receive foreign currency payments, request debit and credit cards, and execute treasury or foreign exchange documents as may be required for the audio licensing and subscription business. The bank must receive a certified copy of this resolution and a written mandate identifying each authorized signatory. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The address set out in the articles of incorporation is hereby adopted as the Company's registered office and principal place of business. The representative director is directed to secure a valid lease or address confirmation, file the registered office with the district court registration office, and notify the National Tax Service for business registration purposes. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The individuals designated in the articles of incorporation as directors are appointed as the statutory directors of the Company. The director named therein as representative director is appointed to that office with authority to bind the Company alone in ordinary business matters. All other directors are appointed as ordinary directors with co-signing authority for banking matters. If the Company's stated capital exceeds the statutory threshold requiring an auditor, the members shall appoint a statutory auditor at the first members meeting. 5. FILINGS AND RATIFICATION. The representative director and any other officer designated by him are authorized to execute and file all incorporation registration applications, obtain the corporate seal authentication certificate, obtain the business registration certificate, make the foreign investment report when required, and onboard the Company with payment service providers. All lawful acts performed by the officers and members before this resolution in furtherance of the Company's formation are hereby ratified, confirmed, and adopted as acts of the Company. This Resolution is effective as of the date of signature by the directors. Each director may sign counterpart copies. ADOPTED this ____ day of __________, 2025, by unanimous written consent of the directors. SIGNED by [Representative Director], Director. SIGNED by [Director], Director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Articles of incorporation drafting, notarization, and foreign investment reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public; Corporate Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the future registered office; Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and foreign exchange banks for foreign investment report matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Korean-law articles of incorporation in the Korean language. The articles must state the corporate name, corporate purpose, total members' equity capital, contribution amount of each member, registered office address, and the method of appointing directors. Every incorporator must sign and seal the articles, and the executed articles must be notarized by a notary public in Korea. If the foreign investment amount reaches the statutory threshold under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, each non-resident investor must file a foreign direct investment report through KOTRA or a domestic foreign exchange bank before or immediately following the court filing. The notary attestation confirms signature authenticity and makes the document acceptable to the court registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized articles of incorporation
Power of attorney granted to a Korean process agent or attorney
Passport copy and overseas address proof of each incorporator
Registered office address certificate or lease memorandum
Foreign direct investment report receipt, if threshold is met
Beneficial ownership statement for each member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses attestation because of mismatched signatures or incomplete objectives, correct the articles, re-execute all signatures, and re-submit to another notary if necessary. If the foreign investment report is suspended, submit a letter of explanation, source-of-funds evidence, and a corrected ownership chart to KOTRA or the issuing foreign exchange bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital contribution deposit and proof of paid-in capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank or authorized securities company in Korea maintaining the contribution deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing for incorporation, each member must fully pay cash into a Korean bank contribution deposit account or fully transfer in-kind property if such contribution is authorized by the articles of incorporation. The depositary bank will issue a deposit certificate or balance confirmation identifying the depositor and the amount. For cash contributions, the funds must remain in the designated account until the corporate registration is completed. If any member fails to contribute, the remaining members are jointly liable for the unpaid amount under the Commercial Act. The deposit certificate and contemporaneous bank statement must be obtained in the name of the representative director designate or the proposed corporate name and will accompany the court filing as proof of paid-in capital.
required_dossiers: Bank-issued capital contribution deposit certificate
Bank statement showing the contribution transaction
In-kind property valuation report and transfer deed, if applicable
Foreign exchange declaration records for funds imported from overseas
Foreign direct investment report acknowledgement, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to issue a certificate because of suspect source of funds, present a declaration of source of wealth and verified transaction records and complete remedial bank KYC. If the court rejects the deposit because the account is held in the wrong title, open a corrected account in the exact proposed legal name and re-deposit before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court registration of incorporation with the district court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office in Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed application for corporation registration to the court registry together with the notarized articles of incorporation, capital contribution deposit certificate, director appointment consents, written resolutions, corporate seal specimen, and a power of attorney if filed by a representative. The registry will verify the legality of the formation, the existence of a genuine office, the total capital entries, and the eligibility of the directors. Upon approval, the court enters the Company in the commercial register and issues a certified copy of the corporate register. Under the Commercial Act, a Yuhan Hoesa is legally established only when the incorporation registration is completed at the principal office; no legal personality exists before that date.
required_dossiers: Completed application for corporation registration
Notarized articles of incorporation
Capital contribution deposit certificate
Consent to appointment and director acceptance documents
Written member or director resolution for establishment
Certified Korean lease confirmation for the main office
Corporate seal specimen certificate
Power of attorney for Korean attorney or authorized filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a request for correction or supplementary documentation, respond within 14 days using the court-prescribed correction form. If the application is rejected for an invalid registered office address, execute a corrected lease or occupancy permit, amend the articles if necessary, and resubmit the complete registration package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service and corporate seal certificate retrieval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the Hometax online portal or the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration is completed, apply to the National Tax Service for a business registration certificate. Provide the certified copy of the commercial register, the corporate seal authentication certificate, the registered office lease agreement, and the representative director's identification. The National Tax Service will issue the business registration certificate, after which the Company must file value-added tax returns on the applicable cycle, issue electronic tax invoices for audio subscription sales, and maintain books for corporate income tax. Because the business is a digital royalty-free stock music licensing platform, no municipal industrial operating license is required, but the Company must confirm that the registered office is a lawful non-residential or mixed-use space permitted for digital commerce.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the commercial register
Corporate seal authentication certificate
Business registration application form
Representative director passport or national ID copy
Lease or address confirmation
Notarized articles of incorporation copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service suspends the business registration application because of discrepancies between the register and the tax form, file a correction through Hometax and resubmit. If the office is deemed an unlicensed residential address, provide a commercial lease or convert the registered office to a permitted commercial space before re-applying.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account activation, payment processor onboarding, and governance record completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank financial crime compliance and KYC unit; Stripe and PayPal merchant compliance teams
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the corporate operating bank account by presenting the corporate seal authentication certificate, the certified copy of commercial register, the business registration certificate, and the board resolution authorizing signatories. The bank will perform KYC review of the representative director, beneficial owners, foreign shareholders, and source of operating funds. After activation, submit the Company formation documents to Stripe and PayPal for merchant onboarding using the exact legal name Yuhan Hoesa, the Korean business registration number, and the proof of bank account. Configure the payment rails to support KRW and USD settlements, electronic tax invoice fields, subscription rebilling, and refund workflows for royalty-free audio content. Maintain the corporate minute book, register of members, and banking mandate as permanent governance records at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal certificate
Certified copy of commercial register
Business registration certificate
Board resolution establishing the banking mandate
Passport and address proof for each bank signatory
Beneficial ownership declaration
Lease proof and bank correspondence
Payment processor application and company background statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines because the board resolution is not sufficiently detailed, issue a supplemental board resolution naming each signatory and each authorized account. If Stripe or PayPal rejects the merchant application, provide a detailed product list, refund policy, copyright ownership statement, digital content terms of use, and the registered corporate purpose in English and Korean.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Digital-only royalty-free stock music licensing and audio sample subscription business under ISIC 5920 with no physical manufacturing, assembly, chemical processing, or warehousing activities; the Company has no installation, discharge source, or environmental footprint requiring a full EIA report or environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the Company generates no wastewater, VOCs, particulate emissions, or hazardous waste streams subject to discharge or emissions limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - the Company operates as a remote digital audio licensing business without a physical industrial workplace; therefore no Civil Defense fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or occupational safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr for business registration, e-Tax Invoice issuance, VAT returns, and tax retrieval services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company): file a Business Registration Application with the district tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered head office before commencing taxable business. Attach the articles of incorporation, proof of shareholder identities, lease or ownership evidence of the place of business, and a corporate bank account certificate. The NTS issues a Business Registration Certificate containing a ten-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the unified Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), VAT registration number, and corporate tax reference number. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic place of business that intends to make taxable supplies in Korea: appoint a statutory tax representative who is a Korean tax accountant or tax attorney, pursuant to the Framework Act on National Taxes. The tax representative must file the same Business Registration Application with the attached power of attorney, the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation or equivalent official company extract in English or certified translation, and a board resolution appointing the tax representative. Once NTS validates the application, the foreign entity is registered in HomeTax and receives a Business Registration Number for VAT purposes. The Business Registration Number must be quoted on all e-Tax Invoices issued in Korea. Registration must occur before the first taxable supply; no economic threshold applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a Korean domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and as an independent VAT taxable person. The Korean tax system does not offer any check-the-box, pass-through, or hybrid mismatch election for a limited liability company. A foreign shareholder may claim treaty benefits on dividends, but the entity level taxation and VAT identity remain fixed.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold. Any person supplying taxable goods or services in Korea, including foreign non-residents, must register for VAT regardless of turnover. A simplified VAT taxpayer status applies only where annual taxable revenue does not exceed KRW 80,000,000, but this status still requires issuance of simplified tax invoices and does not remove the registration mandate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) regime via NTS HomeTax. Every VAT-taxable business must issue an e-Tax Invoice through the HomeTax API or an accredited e-Document provider and transmit it to NTS no later than the day following the supply date. Paper tax invoices are invalid for input VAT deduction. The e-Tax Invoice contains a unique invoice number, tax classification code (including zero-rated export codes), and digital signature. NTS performs post-clearance automated matching and anti-fraud data mining; there is no real-time fiscal stamping device or in-line clearance API, but all invoices must be lodged in the centralized national electronic tax fleet system. Cash receipts are also mandatory for B2C cash transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value Added Tax Act, the supply of royalty-free stock music licensing and audio subscription services qualifies for zero-rating when the service is classified as an 'export of services'. Statutory conditions include: (i) the recipient is a foreign business or a non-resident individual whose habitual residence or place of establishment is outside Korea; (ii) the licensed copyright or music content is exploited outside the Korean customs territory; (iii) the supply is not physically performed at a domestic place of business for Korean-type consumption; and (iv) the consideration is received in a freely convertible foreign currency or through an international payment settlement method, and such foreign exchange receipts are substantiated with approved export documents. For B2B digital services the place of supply is the customer's registered business establishment; for B2C digital services the place of supply is the customer's habitual residence, supported by payment-rail billing address data and device/IP metadata. The supplier must issue a zero-rated e-Tax Invoice in HomeTax, which acts as the export sales declaration for VAT purposes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Zero-rated export e-Tax Invoice issued through HomeTax, explicitly marked as export and including the foreign buyer's name and tax identifier
Digital licensing agreement or purchase order establishing the foreign counterparty, scope of commercial music licensing rights, and the currency-denominated royalty or subscription consideration
Foreign Exchange Acquisition Certificate (Oehoehoekdeukjeungmyeong) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank certifying actual receipt of the foreign currency
SWIFT wire transfer advice, foreign bank statement, or PayPal/Stripe settlement report evidencing cross-border inflow and the net amount credited to the Korean entity's foreign currency account
For B2B transactions, a copy of the overseas business registration certificate or VAT registration number of the recipient
For B2C transactions, customer billing address and payment method evidence (credit card issuer country, device/IP geolocation report) confirming overseas consumption

No customs export declaration is required for purely intangible digital deliveries; if physical media were included, a full Customs Export Declaration and Bill of Lading or Airway Bill would become mandatory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may recharacterize zero-rated export supplies as taxable domestic supplies at 10% VAT if the supporting documentation is incomplete, the foreign-exchange receipt is not substantiated, or the repatriation occurs after 180 days from the supply date. A 'bad claim' penalty of 20% of the incorrectly zero-rated VAT is imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes, in addition to a reporting breach surcharge of 5% to 10% of the tax amount. For fraudulent or fictitious export claims, the aggravating penalty rises to 40% of the unpaid tax, the refunded VAT is clawed back with statutory interest, and criminal liability may be pursued under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. All export evidence must be retained for at least five years from the filing deadline of the relevant VAT return.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, operating as monetary and central banking authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the policy direction of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is freely convertible for current account transactions, including digital content licensing and subscription service exports. Payments for such services may be received in foreign currency and retained in a domestic foreign-currency account without mandatory surrender. Capital account transactions, by contrast, are subject to reporting or prior approval under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; a foreign investor subscribing to shares of a Yuhan Hoesa must file an FDI report through KOTRA or an authorized foreign exchange bank and obtain a foreign investment registration certificate before the capital remittance is considered compliant. Dividend and royalty profit remittance is permitted, but the bank will require evidence of tax clearance, audited financial statements, and a board resolution confirming distribution. The practical hurdle for a new digital music entity is not government exchange rationing but bank risk appetite: recurring micro-royalty inflows from Stripe and PayPal can generate automatic transaction monitoring alerts unless the company maintains a clean audit trail of the underlying license agreements and end-user records. For a digital audio business, the convertibility regime is favorable provided all current account inward remittances are settled through a licensed foreign exchange bank and all capital movements are pre-notified to the Bank of Korea or the delegated foreign exchange bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory percentage of export receipts must be surrendered into Korean won; the mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 0%. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export and service proceeds must be received within one year from the date of export or service performance, and this collection window may be extended by up to six months with foreign exchange bank approval. Foreign currency receipts may be held in domestic foreign-currency deposit accounts. For the royalty-free stock music business, subscription and licence fees collected through Stripe or PayPal must be aggregated and repatriated through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank within the statutory window.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: KRW Operational Account with attached Foreign Currency Settlement Account and Capital Escrow Account
Corporate Multi-Currency Account with Capital Escrow Facility
Foreign Investor Capital Account plus Operational KRW Account
KRW Current Account and Foreign Currency Deposit Account package

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary banking engine. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, Revolut Business, and Airwallex are not licensed foreign exchange banks under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and therefore cannot satisfy the statutory settlement, reporting, and foreign investment escrow requirements for a domestic Korean entity. Their viability is medium only as auxiliary collection or disbursement vehicles that funnel funds into a licensed domestic bank account; all final settlement and outward remittance must be executed through a Tier-1 domestic foreign exchange bank. EMIs are legally permissible for ancillary payment aggregation, but they are not a substitute for a Korean corporate bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is effectively mandatory for the statutory director and authorised signatories when opening a corporate account for a Yuhan Hoesa. Korean banking practice under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act requires face-to-face identification by the bank's compliance officer; there is no general remote video or consular proxy opening for foreign directors. Some banks allow a Korean-resident director or locally appointed attorney to complete the interview if the foreign director executes a notarised power of attorney, but the signatory authority will still be scrutinised. The recommended path is a physical visit by the statutory director to a Seoul branch with original corporate documents, company seal, apostilled UBO identification, and a board resolution naming all bank signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed Korean entity with a non-resident sole shareholder, no operating history, and no audited financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, complete share registry, notarised UBO declaration for every natural person with 25% or more ownership, notarised passport copies, board resolution appointing directors and bank signatories, source-of-funds documentation for the shareholder's investment, and a certified English translation of the foreign investment report or KOTRA receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring low-value microtransactions from Stripe and PayPal with payer identities that may not be immediately visible to the Korean bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML transaction monitoring framework, sample end-user licensing agreement, merchant statements and settlement reports from Stripe/PayPal, platform sales dashboard, data protection and data sharing agreements with payment aggregators, and a written undertaking to make the underlying subscription and licence records available to the bank compliance committee on request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty distributions to overseas music producers that could be interpreted as profit stripping or unlicensed remittance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed royalty and licensing contracts naming each beneficiary, tax invoices and Korean withholding tax certificates, producer payment schedule, revenue share policy approved by the board, and a legal opinion from Korean tax counsel confirming arm's length royalty rates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming foreign currency wires into a newly opened domestic account without immediate commercial justification, triggering a suspicious transaction report
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan with cash flow projections, existing customer or marketplace agreements, pro-forma revenue forecast by territory, foreign investment registration certificate for capital injections, copies of all inbound SWIFT MT103 messages with payment purpose codes, and a commitment to file monthly Bank of Korea current account transaction reports through the designated foreign exchange bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign capital contributions must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or an authorised foreign exchange bank before the inbound wire is credited to a dedicated foreign-invested enterprise foreign currency account. The wire instruction should reference the foreign investment report number and use a corporate capital contribution purpose code; after receipt, the bank issues a foreign investment registration certificate and a Korean certified public accountant performs capital verification. For operating revenue from audio licensing, inbound SWIFT MT103 wires must be settled as current account service export payments with the underlying licence agreement attached; capital codes must not be used for commercial subscription receipts. All net proceeds should be swept from Stripe and PayPal into the domestic foreign currency settlement account within the statutory reporting period, then converted to KRW only when operational cash is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty and producer payments should be executed through the domestic foreign exchange bank as standard outward SWIFT MT103 remittances after verification of the payee, the underlying licensing contract, the royalty calculation, and the required Korean withholding tax payment certificate. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not appropriate for digital audio licensing and are reserved for physical goods trade; instead, the company should use ordinary bank transfers for low-value producer payouts. If mass payouts are made through PayPal or a similar channel, the company should first aggregate the total abroad or in the domestic settlement account and execute one swept outward remittance to avoid fragmented high-frequency transactions that would distort the bank's transaction monitoring risk score.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD or KRW/EUR plain-vanilla deliverable forward contracts permitted for substantiated future export and royalty receivables at a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank within the bank's credit approval limits

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts restricted to institutional participants with proven real underlying export exposure; Korean resident companies are generally prohibited from using offshore NDF markets for speculative positioning

Cross-currency swaps permitted only when matched to actual foreign currency liabilities or contracted receivables, with all swap economics reported to the Bank of Korea through the delegated foreign exchange bank
Deliverable currency options and collars permitted on a cautious basis when supported by a documented commercial pipeline of subscription and licensing receipts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (including the audited or unaudited financial statements as annexed statutory schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December fiscal year-end, by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or understated corporate income triggers additional tax of 10-30% of the omitted amount plus 0.022% per day late-payment interest; chronic delinquency leads to asset seizure, business closure, and after more than 5 years of inactivity, a court order of dissolution striking the entity from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surcharge (local surtax on corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government (City/Province) via the NTS joint filing windows
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax return; for a December fiscal year-end, by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge on unpaid surtax, daily late-interest at 0.022%, with compulsory collection and registration of tax lien against corporate assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By July 25 of the calendar year for the January 1 to June 30 tax period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of the shortage for incorrect returns (20% for fraudulent omission or false registration) plus 0.022% per day late-payment interest; repeat non-filing may subject the taxpayer to enforced assessment, seizure of bank accounts, and business premises closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 25 of the next calendar year for the July 1 to December 31 tax period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same as first half-year: additional tax of 10-20% of uncovered amount, daily late-payment interest of 0.022%, enforced collection, and possible business closure for persistent delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Approval of Financial Statements (annual statutory meeting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate record maintained at registered office; subject to inspection by Korean Commercial Act authorities or court on demand.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (e.g., for a December fiscal year-end, by March 31).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual general meeting does not create a direct tax fine but entitles any shareholder to request the court to order a meeting; directors can be subject to administrative fines under the Commercial Act of up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,700), and the entity’s continued failure to perform statutory corporate functions may be treated as a ground for dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Submission (only where statutory audit threshold is exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) audit-manager system and the National Tax Service via the corporate tax return packet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor must issue the report and submit it to the company before the annual shareholders' meeting; for December fiscal year-end entities, by March 31 (tax return deadline) at the latest.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission of a mandated external audit report results in Critical Audit Deficiency sanctions, public registration of violations, fines up to KRW 50 billion for gross negligence in audit duties, and in severe cases the auditor’s license suspension; for the company, the audited financial statements cannot be validly approved at the shareholders' meeting and may be disregarded by tax authorities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies etc. (as amended), mandatory appointment of a certified public accountant auditor is triggered by: (i) listing on a Korean stock exchange or filing a listing registration statement; (ii) total assets at the most recent balance sheet date exceeding KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9 million); (iii) being a financial institution, holding company, or other business designated by the Financial Services Commission for public-interest audit even below the asset threshold; (iv) being ordered by the FSC in the public interest for regulatory or prudential reasons. No separate revenue or headcount-based audit threshold applies to an ordinary private Yuhan Hoesa; the balance-sheet asset test is the decisive quantitative trigger.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea mandates K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, converged with IFRS) for listed companies and certain specified entities. A private Yuhan Hoesa within the SME classification may apply the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), including the simplified accounting standards for small and medium-sized companies (SME Standards), which are aligned with the IFRS for SMEs framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Korean Commercial Act does not require an annual UBO confirmation filing for a private Yuhan Hoesa. Nevertheless, the company must keep an accurate member register at its registered office, and any shareholding transfer must be endorsed in that register before it becomes effective against the company; to become opposable to third parties, the transfer must be recorded in the member register without delay. In addition, if an acquisition involves a non-resident investor, a report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act is due to the Ministry of Economy and Finance or delegated institution within 30 days of the transaction. Consequently, the practical compliance window is 30 days for equity changes involving foreign participants and immediate same-day updating for domestic transfers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 800 per annum for a standard registered office service in Seoul/Busan; annual corporate secretarial agent fees range from USD 1,000 to USD 2,500 based on task complexity.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 15,000 per annum for a small-to-mid-sized Korean entity within the compulsory audit zone, depending on transaction volume and K-GAAP/K-IFRS complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; combined with the 10% local income tax surcharge the top effective marginal rate is 26.4%. Lower brackets apply at 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean R&D tax credits under the Special Tax Reduction and Exemption Act, tax credits for job creation and facility investment, and reduced taxes for foreign-invested technology enterprises in certain free economic zones; no patent box regime applies to digital stock-music royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Tax Base and Self-Assessment) under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act; electronically filed through HomeTax, the National Tax Service e-File portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the last day of the third month following the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end the return is due March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension is available by filing an extension application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer entity identification and non-resident ownership schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The Korean LLC's corporate registration number, head office location, business purpose, and equity ownership breakdown.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the domestic entity as a Korean resident corporation for worldwide taxation. Disclose the country of residence, ownership percentage, and taxpayer identification of each non-resident shareholder so that the National Tax Service can assess whether the 22% aggregate dividend withholding rate or a reduced treaty rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Book income to tax base reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Starting book income before tax, adjusted for non-taxable revenue, non-deductible expenses, and deferred tax items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all royalty-free stock-music subscription and digital licensing fees earned from Korean and cross-border licensees as Korean-source income if the customer or use occurs in Korea. Do not exclude revenue merely because it was settled through Stripe or PayPal; all gross proceeds must be recognized in won and reconciled to form data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D credits, foreign tax credits, and other statutory reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean domestic corporation cannot claim credits on behalf of non-resident shareholders. Any foreign withholding taxes passed through the LLC must be supported by a foreign tax credit reconciliation schedule; treaty reduction of Korean corporate tax is not available to a domestic corporation absent a specific domestic tax law provision.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Corporate income tax calculation and local income tax surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive national corporate income tax rates and the 10% local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute national corporate tax, then add 10% of that amount as local income tax. The corporate tax base must be reported in Korean won; no foreign currency election is permitted for a domestic entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Outbound withholding tax declaration for non-resident payees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax computation on dividends, interest, royalties, and fees paid to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC is the statutory withholding agent for non-resident shareholders and license suppliers. Withhold 22% aggregate on dividend, interest, and royalty remittances unless a valid DTA application has been approved before payment. Report each payee's country, certificate, and beneficial ownership status in the attached schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of controlled transactions involving intercompany license fees, management fees, and revenue allocations to overseas affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each related-party stock-music licensor or licensee, the royalty rate, and the intercompany transaction value in Korean won. A warning note must appear if the controlled transaction volume exceeds the documentation threshold; failure to attach the required transfer pricing schedules converts the return into an unfaithful filing and triggers penalty surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or false filing under Article 75 of the Corporate Tax Act: added tax of 20% of unpaid tax for non-filing, 40% for unfaithful filing, daily overdue interest at the National Tax Service statutory rate, and a separate penalty for failure to withhold outbound non-resident tax. Intentional underreporting of music licensing revenue can be referred for prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act with imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to twice the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory dividend withholding tax on remittances to non-resident shareholders: 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remitting dividends, the non-resident recipient must submit a Treaty Reduction/Exemption Application to the National Tax Service through HomeTax, attaching a tax residency certificate issued by the shareholder's country of residence, a signed beneficial ownership declaration, evidence of economic substance and ultimate control, and source documentation proving entitlement to the royalty, interest, or dividend. The National Tax Service compares the applicant's substance with the treaty's limitation on benefits articles; a conduit or mailbox recipient is denied relief and the full 22% statutory rate is withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for cross-border royalties and related-party interest is 22% aggregate; under many Korean double tax treaties the rate is reduced to 15% or less, for example under the U.S.-Korea convention royalties and interest are generally reduced to 15%, provided the payee is the beneficial owner and the main purpose of the payment arrangement is not treaty shopping.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion for cross-border related-party controlled transactions triggering the Local File; KRW 10 billion for domestic related-party transactions; Master File is required when the consolidated worldwide group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report obligations follow the International Tax Adjustment Act thresholds for groups exceeding KRW 100 billion in consolidated revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies a substance-over-form doctrine under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the International Tax Adjustment Act. A Yuhan Hoesa licensing marketplace must maintain actual office space, employees, servers, contracts, invoicing, and income-generating decision-making in Korea; if the company is merely a shell for licensing royalties from foreign stock-music assets or for shifting profit to foreign shareholders, the National Tax Service will disregard the entity, reattribute its income, and deny treaty benefits under the anti-abuse doctrine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: When the Korean LLC underreports subscription and royalty revenue from the stock-music business by omitting Stripe or PayPal settlement data, depositing customer fees into foreign personal accounts, or booking personal expenditures as deductible business costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Crimes Act Article 3: imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine not exceeding twice the tax evaded; corporate income tax deficiency reassessed together with a 40% penalty surcharge for unfaithful filing and daily overdue interest; the entity also becomes ineligible for tax clearance certificates and bank transaction credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed the concealment face joint and several civil liability for the unpaid corporate tax and surcharges under the Commercial Act; criminal indictment for tax fraud may include imprisonment, permanent bar from corporate management, and placement on the National Tax Service departure restriction blacklist.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Treaty Shopping Shell Conduit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC artificially charges below-market royalty rates to foreign related licensees, or the company is established without real staff and operations solely to route stock-music royalty payments to a foreign parent and claim reduced DTA withholding on outbound distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 4 and 12 authorize the National Tax Service to recharacterize the intercompany transaction at an arm's-length royalty rate and reassess tax; additional taxes of 20% for deficient documentation and 40% for false or undocumented transactions apply; the DTA benefit is denied and 22% statutory withholding is assessed retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign sham intercompany agreements or knowingly maintain an economic-substance shell breach their duty of loyalty and due diligence under the Commercial Act; a court may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for restitution, impose travel bans, and impose criminal imprisonment for fraudulent treaty shopping.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The stock-music marketplace accepts high-volume subscriptions from foreign customers through U.S. payment processors and settles the funds into Korean bank accounts without filing the required foreign-exchange transaction declarations, without beneficial-owner verification of the corporate shareholders, and without reporting suspicious transfers that correspond to royalty pass-throughs to foreign shell companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial Transaction Reports Act Article 12 and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Article 28: failure to report suspicious transactions or unlawful cross-border settlement is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years and/or a fine up to KRW 100 million; the National Tax Service may reconstruct omitted Korean-source revenue and assess corporate tax plus penalties and interest on all unreported settlement amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who control payment routing and approve foreign-exchange settlement may be criminally prosecuted, jointly liable for the unreported funds and tax deficiencies, placed on the departure blacklist, and disqualified from continuing corporate management because the entity is treated as their alter ego.
